bp._: Compiled 2026-10-16. FCR/FHR/FBR rows: Maxroll 'Breakpoints & Animations' (Teo1904, updated 2026-02-10) https://maxroll.gg/d2/resources/breakpoints-animations, recomputed from its formulas and matched row-for-row against it, then against the Steam community guide 'FHR, FCR, FBR Breakpoints Guide' (IDK, 2026-02-18/19) https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails?id=3669140110 (all agree; Steam omits only the theoretical tail rows) and D2Runewizard https://d2runewizard.com/breakpoints (agrees except it swaps the Druid werewolf and werebear FCR columns). IAS: Maxroll 'Attack Speed' (MacroBioBoi, 2026-02-10) https://maxroll.gg/d2/resources/attack-speed; base frames, action frames, caps and rounding read from the diablo2.io Attack Speed Calculator v1.57 source (a fork of Warren's IAS calculator, 'D2R & RotW 3.3') https://diablo2.io/attackspeed.php , https://diablo2.io/styles/zulu/theme/js/ias/constants.js and calculator.js. WSM and weapon class checked against game-data/vanilla-93847/data/global/excel/weapons.txt (build 3.3.93847). The Amazon Basin (amazonbasin.com) is a parked domain and its classic.battle.net pages are not in the Wayback Machine, so it was not read directly; diablo2.io's tables descend from the same lineage. Rows are [pct, frames] with the 0% row first; each row is the lowest gear % that reaches that frame count. FHR/FBR rows above ~600% (and the Assassin/Barbarian/Paladin 4680 FHR row) are theoretical, not reachable by gear.

conventions.fcrCap: FCR is capped by EFCR 75, i.e. 200% FCR; rows past 200 would add nothing and are not listed.

weaponKeys.fhr.Druid.human_1h_swinging: weapons.txt wclass 1hs on a one-handed item (axe, club, mace, scepter, sword, wand, throwing axe). Maxroll/Steam list these types.
weaponKeys.fhr.Paladin.spear_staff: Maxroll says 'Spears and Staves'. INFERRED: the animation class is wclass 2ht or stf; stf also holds polearms and two-handed axes/maces and no source says whether those count.
weaponKeys.fbr.Amazon.one_handed_swinging: Maxroll: axes, clubs, maces, hammers, scepters, swords, throwing axes (and wands in the cast-rate text). Javelins and knives are 1ht and use default.
weaponKeys.fcr.Amazon: Cast FRAMES are weapon-independent for the Amazon; only the action frame varies with the weapon, so one table.

conventions.noWeaponSplit: Amazon and Assassin FHR have a single table (no spear/staff split in any source). Assassin FBR has one table and applies to claw weapon block and shield block. The weapon-dependent splits are Paladin FHR, Druid FHR, Amazon FBR.
conventions.actionFlags: Cast-delay action frames are omitted. Maxroll's published action-flag rows do not reproduce from its own 'Base Action Flag' table for Druid forms and vampire form.

formulas.EFx: EFCR = EFHR = EFBR = floor(120*X/(X+120))  (X = total gear % of that stat)
formulas.fcr: frames = ceil(256*CastBase / floor(AnimSpeed*(100+min(EFCR,75))/100)) - 1; Sorceress Lightning and Chain Lightning drop the '- 1'
formulas.fhr_fbr: frames = ceil(256*Base / floor(AnimSpeed*(50+EFx)/100)) - 1; Holy Shield adds 50 to EFBR

params.caveat: Maxroll's printed CastBase column lists Druid 16 and Necromancer 15; its own tables (and the Steam and D2Runewizard tables) only reproduce with Druid 15 and Necromancer 16, so the two look swapped there. The values above are the ones that reproduce every published row.

formulas.verified: Recomputed from these formulas, every published Maxroll cast, hit-recovery and block table matches row-for-row on the frame column (Druid forms, vampire form and Lightning included). Maxroll's worked examples reproduce: Sorceress 50 FCR = 10 frames, Lightning = 15, Sorceress 50 FHR = 9, Paladin 50 FBR = 3, with Holy Shield = 2.

ias.formula: frames = ceil( 256*(AnimLength - StartFrame) / floor( AnimSpeed*(100 + clamp(SIAS + EIAS - WSM, -85, 75)) / 100 ) ) - 1, where EIAS = floor(120*IAS/(120+IAS)). The code (diablo2.io calculator.js) clamps the whole (SIAS - WSM + EIAS) term; Maxroll writes it as AnimRate(100) + SIAS + EIAS - WSM.

terms.AnimLength: the class's unmodified attack animation length in frames for the weapon's animation class (baseFrames[*].frames below)
terms.AnimSpeed: 256 for almost everything (a fixed-point 1.0, to cut rounding error). Exceptions: Assassin claws (ht1) 208, or 227 when the animation length is 12 (2.5 PTR change); Laying Traps 128; Vampire form 176 with AnimLength 14; Undead Fetish form 256 with 12; Druid werewolf/werebear use the shapeshift equation below
terms.IAS: the sum of increased attack speed on items, plus the weapon's own IAS only if it is the main-hand weapon; off-hand weapon IAS is ignored
terms.EIAS: IAS after diminishing returns, floor(120*IAS/(120+IAS)), so 75 EIAS needs 225 IAS
terms.SIAS: skill and aura attack speed (Fanaticism, Burst of Speed, Werewolf, Frenzy, Maul), added undiminished; slows (Decrepify, Holy Freeze, chill, 'Slows Target') subtract
terms.WSM: weapons.txt column `speed` (col 25; blank = 0); positive is slower. Subtracted, so a negative WSM adds speed directly
terms.StartFrame: frames skipped at the start of the animation; per diablo2.io code only the Amazon and Sorceress on the standard attack, Fend and Zeal: 1 unarmed, 2 with a weapon (1hs, 2hs, 1ht, 2ht, stf). Every other class and skill: 0
terms.-1: overlap of the last and first frames when attacks chain; not applied to sequence skills (Jab, Impale, Fists of Fire, Claws of Thunder, Blades of Ice, Dragon Claw, Double Swing, Double Throw, Frenzy), Zeal, Fend, Strafe, Fury, Dragon Talon or Whirlwind

ias.rounding: EIAS floors; AnimSpeed*(100+E)/100 floors; the quotient rounds UP; then subtract 1.

caps.note: The 75 cap applies to the whole SIAS - WSM + EIAS term in the diablo2.io code, so a -30 WSM weapon starts at +30. The cap was missing for a short period of D2R (calculator.js comment); 75 is current. No frame floor is stated in any source; practical floors come from the caps (FCR 200, EIAS 75) and the formula itself.

skillIas.sequenceSkills: sequence skills carry an extra -30 to SIAS (Impale's +30 cancels it); Maxroll words it as WSM+30 and no -1
skillIas.throwing: a throw skill carries a flat -30 (not the Barbarian)

ias.specialForms: Rollback skills (Zeal, Fend, Strafe, Fury, Dragon Talon) have per-hit lengths, and the dual-wield Barbarian and Assassin skills use VInc: use the Maxroll Attack Speed page or the calculator. Since 2.4 werewolf and werebear take the faster of the primary equation and the shapeshift equation AnimSpeed = floor(256*FramesNeutral/Delay), Delay = floor(256*FramesChar/((100+WIAS-WSM)*CharSpeed/100)) (FramesNeutral 13 wolf, 12 bear; FramesChar 15; CharSpeed 256).

weaponClassMap.source: game-data/vanilla-93847/data/global/excel/weapons.txt: column `wclass` (col 42) names the animation class of a one-handed grip and `2handedwclass` (col 43) that of a two-handed grip. Observed: 1hs, 1ht, 2ht, stf, bow, xbw, ht1, and 2hs for 18 two-handed swords whose wclass is 1hs. Fields `type` and `type2` give the item type.
weaponClassMap.rule: Use wclass when the weapon is held one-handed (or in a one-hand-only class), and 2handedwclass when held two-handed. Matters for the Barbarian (a 2hs sword held in one hand uses 1hs) and for the Warlock Book + two-handed sword grip.
weaponClassMap.charstats: charstats.txt column `baseWClass` is hth for all classes including the Warlock
weaponClassMap.check: All 283 weapons.txt rows that share a name with the diablo2.io weapon list agree on WSM (`speed`) and on the wclass/2handedwclass-to-class map. The other nine differ only in spelling: weapons.txt's table name against the game's display string, or trailing spaces.

ias.baseFramesFields: frames = AnimLength of the standard attack; actionFrame = frame on which the hit lands (hit/damage, used by Zeal, Strafe and Fend); altFrames = the alternate standard-attack animation some class/weapon pairs alternate with (Assassin hth and ht1: 12, Paladin 2hs: 19)
ias.throwFrames: base.*.throw.frames is the throw animation (a plain integer in the source, no action frame); the Barbarian's two-weapon skills are handled by the calculator

mercBaseFrames.note: diablo2.io marks Rogue, Desert Mercenary and Bash/Frenzy Barbarian unarmed values 'assumed'; treat as unverified

workedExamples.note: Maxroll writes it with AnimLength 12 and gets 11; the diablo2.io code gets 12 via 13 base frames minus StartFrame 1. Same answer.

workedExamples.source: computed here with the same formula; NO source states this number
workedExamples.case: Paladin, Phase Blade (WSM -30), standard attack 1hs, 0 IAS
workedExamples.note: 11 at 0 IAS, then 10 at 8 IAS, 9 at 24, 8 at 54. No source confirms a separate Phase Blade figure for Zeal.

d2rChanges.2.4: Druid werewolf and werebear take the faster of the primary and shapeshift equations (Maxroll Attack Speed changelog, 4 Feb 2022). Pattern and Guardian Angel gain Faster Block Rate (Maxroll Breakpoints changelog, 12 Feb 2022). The 75 EIAS cap exists in D2R (diablo2.io source comment).
d2rChanges.2.5 PTR: Assassin claw animations AIA2HT1 and AIA2HT2 changed AnimSpeed from 208 to 227 for the 12-frame variant (diablo2.io source comment, not Blizzard notes).
d2rChanges.sorceressLightning: I found no change to the Lightning / Chain Lightning table: the breakpoints 0/7/15/23/35/52/78/117/194 are identical in Maxroll (2026-02), the Steam guide and D2Runewizard. The only D2R-specific nuance is that the Lightning formula drops the '- 1' and uses a 19-frame base.
d2rChanges.barbarianAssassin: I found no Barbarian or Assassin FCR/FHR/FBR table change in the 2.4 or 2.5 notes I could fetch; current tables match the classic ones given in the sources.

warlock.confidence: medium: community sources only, no Blizzard publication or datamine found
warlock.claim: The Warlock uses the Necromancer's cast, hit-recovery and block frame tables (and, in diablo2.io's calculator, its attack frames too).
warlock.source: diablo2.io Attack Speed Calculator 'D2R & RotW 3.3': 'Warlock casting/HR/block/kick/throw matches Necromancer; Cleave and Mirrored Blades are not included yet (hardcoded sequences awaiting datamine)' and constants.js resolveCharacter(WARLOCK) -> NECROMANCER (https://diablo2.io/attackspeed.php). Corroborated by Maxroll's Warlock build guides, which target 75% and 125% FCR (https://maxroll.gg/d2/guides/echoing-strike-warlock-guide, abyss-warlock-build-guide, blood-boil-warlock-guide, fire-warlock-guide) and 26% / 56% FHR; the Steam guide https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails?id=3669140110 (Feb 2026), AOEAH https://www.aoeah.com/news/4399--d2r-warlock-fcr-ias-fhr-fbr-breakpoints--calculation (2026-02-24, says its IAS is not pinned down), D2Runewizard https://d2runewizard.com/breakpoints and d2rwiki https://d2rwiki.com/guides/warlock-breakpoints (Aug 2026, itself citing the others) all list the Necromancer values.
warlock.ias: use Necromancer baseFrames (also what diablo2.io does); unconfirmed. Cleave and Mirrored Blades attack sequences are not tabulated by any source.
doubts: Steam's Warlock FHR list stops at 152 (no 377) and its FBR list at 174 (no 600); these are listing cuts, not different values, but they are the only visible Warlock-vs-Necromancer difference in any source.

Maxroll's Mirrored Blades Warlock guide recommends a 48% FHR breakpoint; 48 is not a Necromancer FHR row (its rows run 39, 56). That guide's page may have copied a melee-class figure, or the melee Warlock may use a different hit-recovery table. Unresolved.
Nobody has published the animdata frame counts; the local game-data folder has no animdata, so this cannot be checked here.
